About me The name “Wild Acorn” comes from how I think about film. An acorn grows into a tree, while an image is only a fragment of time. People change, people age, but certain moments remain — like seeds — waiting to be encountered again at some point in the future. At the same time, an acorn suggests a beginning. The start of something that takes root, and slowly unfolds over time. This is close to how I understand moving images. Not as a finished, carefully packaged result, but as a record of something just beginning. My approach is largely documentary rather than staged.
